_comment: The Project=voicenotes tag query - the only way candidates are ever identified
(§10.3: never a wildcard, never a name match). One entry per classification the
script can reach, so the plan is an exhaustive statement of its behaviour:
voicenotes-api-dev            claimed by voicenotes-dev -> skipped
voicenotes-worker-dev         claimed by voicenotes-dev -> skipped
voicenotes-ingest-dev         unclaimed, prefixed         -> DELETE (the orphan a
rollback leaves when a logical resource is removed
from the template but its physical resource survives)
voicenotes-api-prod           unclaimed, prefixed, other instance -> DELETE, and
filtered out by --instance dev
voicenotes-probe-dev          unclaimed, prefixed, Protected=true -> refused, and
refused ONLY by that tag: it is otherwise identical
to the orphan above. Without it the Protected gate is
untestable, because the table and bucket are already
refused for holding the corpus and would keep the test
green with the gate deleted
passbook-notifier             MISTAGGED Project=voicenotes -> refused by the
name-prefix veto. This is the entry that proves the
tag alone never authorizes a delete (G-067)
table voicenotes-dev          Protected=true              -> refused first of all
the data bucket               corpus + audio (I1, I2)     -> refused, erasure only
the user pool                 identities                  -> refused
/aws/lambda/voicenotes-ingest-dev  log group               -> reported: deleting it
outside CloudFormation is denied to this principal
role/voicenotes-ingest-dev    same                        -> reported. Roles and
functions share a name in the template, so the
stranded function's role carries the same name
the HTTP API                  opaque identifier           -> reported
group voicenotes              CLAIMED by the bootstrap stack, and NOT named
voicenotes-* -> proves the claim check runs before
the prefix veto, or the sweep would propose deleting
the Resource Group teardown verifies itself against
stack voicenotes-dev-failed   a stack is Category A's business -> skipped here
